title: High-field Josephson effect enabled by a moiré Hofstadter spectrum
why_careful: Four junctions with a second device (GH2) reproducing the high-field pockets and the null devices GH3-GH4 reported, a non-moiré graphene control junction, normal-state Fabry-Pérot checks under voltage bias, normal-state Landau fans with the supercurrent quenched by a 200 nA bias, and an explicit Ic extraction rule.

spans:
The principal observations reported here were reproduced across multiple additional
devices with different twist angles and geometries (see Supplementary Information), however in
the following we focus on device GH1, which has a twist angle θ ∼ 0.21 ± 0.01◦ , junction length
L ∼ 200 nm, and width W ∼ 1.5 µm.

No high field superconductivity nor clear Fabry-Pérot oscillations were observed for the other
two devices GH3 and GH4. This can be expected, as their much longer lengths lead to very low
critical currents (see Table S1, Fig. S4c-d and Fig. S8d).
info.why: these sentences say how many devices were measured, which one is shown and that two of four showed no high-field supercurrent

extracted from Fig. 1e as the d.c. bias current I at which dV /dI reaches 50% of RN .

To relate the theoretical model to our experimental results, we use the base-temperature zero-bias
conductance 1/R as a proxy for the onset of the superconducting phase, i.e. finite junction critical
current.
